dish.title: Irish Beef and Stout Stew with Potatoes and Carrots
dish.description: Chunks of beef chuck browned and slowly simmered in Irish stout with onions, carrots, potatoes, tomato paste, and thyme until the meat is spoon-tender and the gravy is dark and glossy. Served with crusty bread.

recipe_version.title: Irish Beef and Stout Stew with Potatoes and Carrots
recipe_version.description: Chunks of beef chuck browned and slowly simmered in Irish stout with onions, carrots, potatoes, tomato paste, and thyme until the meat is spoon-tender and the gravy is dark and glossy. Served with crusty bread.

ingredients.name: crusty bread
ingredients.display_name: crusty bread whose label lists no milk, butter, egg, soy, or sesame

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Cube the beef, pat it dry, season with 1 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper, and toss with the flour. Chop the onions, mince the garlic, cut the carrots and potatoes, and chop the parsley.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.body: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a 6-quart Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown the beef in three batches, about 5 minutes per batch, adding the last 1 tbsp oil as needed. Transfer to a bowl.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.body: Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onions until soft and browned, about 6 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the beef
steps.body: Pour in the stout and scrape the bottom, then add 2 cups water, the thyme, bay leaves, brown sugar, 1 tsp salt, and the beef with its juices. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently 1 1/2 hours.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.body: Add the carrots and potatoes, cover, and simmer until they and the beef are tender, about 45 minutes. Uncover for the last 10 of those minutes to thicken the gravy.

steps.title: Slice the bread
steps.body: While the stew simmers, slice the bread (overlap stated).

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves. Ladle the stew into bowls, scatter the parsley, and serve with bread.

coverage_contribution: First Irish dish. A classic dark beef stew; stews are not among the heavy clusters (soups are).
near_duplicate_review: Compared with cottage-pie: whole beef chunks in a stout gravy, not minced beef under mash. Compared with german-beef-rouladen in this wave: cubed stewing beef with potatoes in the pot, not stuffed rolls. Compared with slow-cooker-ropa-vieja: dark stout gravy, potatoes, and carrots, not shredded beef in tomato and peppers.
